operator_locked_immediate_priorities: P0-A: normal nonterminal turn worktime at least 10 minutes (600 observed elapsed seconds)
P0-B: SAME MAIN normal close at ACTUAL END + exactly 1 minute (60 seconds)

execution_envelope.distinction: The 10-minute (600-second) bounded execution turn is not the 15-minute (900-second) P0 acceptance window.

startup_measurement.rule: Preserve raw historical samples; classify current generations prospectively only from observed boundaries. Invocation metadata alone is not BOOT_STARTED or first useful work.

active_retest.purpose: Prospectively verify the operator-locked two-part P0 without broad product expansion.
active_retest.success_signal: At least 10 minutes (600 seconds) observed elapsed on a normal CONTINUE turn with chained real work, followed by SAME MAIN live-verified at ACTUAL END + exactly 1 minute (60 seconds); provider delivery/startup measured separately.
active_retest.failure_signal: Voluntary normal close before 10 minutes (600 seconds), provisional/natural-hourly due left as normal successor, any interpretation of 60 as 60 minutes, inconsistent durable due projection, or fabricated useful time.

latest_diagnosis.evidence: Epoch 81 proved one 678-second normal turn and one exact 1-minute (60-second) SAME MAIN close. Operator identified ambiguous unitless timing as a plausible schedule interpretation defect and reprioritized sustained worktime plus reservation renewal above product breadth.
latest_diagnosis.implication: Require consecutive live evidence for both P0-A and P0-B; keep all critical human-readable time units explicit and provider delay separate.

next_corrective_experiment.hypothesis: Explicit-unit schedule semantics plus a hard 10-minute (600-second) work floor can make normal continuation behavior reproducible without adding product breadth.
next_corrective_experiment.success_signal: Consecutive normal turns reproduce both sustained worktime and exact SAME MAIN ACTUAL END + 1 minute (60 seconds) close.
